rules.message: Organize modules around responsibility (style guide, section 6): this is past the project's size or complexity limit.
rules.fix: Split the function or file by responsibility behind a small interface; keep behaviour and the public API unchanged.

rules.message: Represent absence and failure in the type (style guide, section 2): unwrap() panics on ordinary failure.
rules.fix: Return a Result or Option with `?`, or handle the case. In an inline #[cfg(test)] module this is fine.

rules.message: expect() is for a broken invariant, not for ordinary failure (style guide, section 2).
rules.fix: Return the error to the caller, or make the message say which invariant holds and why.

rules.message: Panicking for ordinary failure is a common trap (style guide, section 11).
rules.fix: Return an error the caller can handle; panic only on a bug.

rules.message: Unfinished code: todo!() and unimplemented!() panic when reached.
rules.fix: Finish the code, or return an error that says what is not supported.

rules.message: dbg!() is for local debugging and must not be committed.
rules.fix: Remove it, or log through the crate's tracing/logging.

rules.message: Library crates do not print: callers decide what reaches the terminal.
rules.fix: Return the value or an event, or use tracing/logging.

rules.message: A library must not end the process; it skips destructors and takes the decision from the caller.
rules.fix: Return an error and let the binary decide how to exit.

rules.message: Treat unsafe code as a contract (style guide, section 10).
rules.fix: Keep the block as small as possible and put a `// SAFETY:` comment above it saying why each assumption holds.

rules.message: Making everything public is a common trap (style guide, sections 4 and 11): a glob re-export widens the public API silently.
rules.fix: Re-export the items callers need, by name.

rules.text: Prefer clear ownership and message passing over Arc<Mutex<_>>; reach for shared mutable state only when the design needs it, and keep locks short (style guide, section 9).
Library crates return typed errors (thiserror-style enums) that say what failed; add context at boundaries instead of turning errors into strings early (style guide, section 7).
